source_record.bounded_interface_domain: The exact shared item, configuration, time horizon, population and actually used receiving premise in the member are identified. source_record.domain_horizon_authority: Each exact object in the member, with actual horizon and decision rights established rather than presumed from the lineage label.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Conditional analytical receiving consequence; no whole-predicate entailment, empirical net benefit, universal option method, current legal determination or new historical descent.
source_record.native_common_basis: Prospective continuation, stopping and retirement compare beneficiary effects, option value, transition and external costs under actual authority; sunk costs and indirect value are not conflated.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Evaluation, switching, abandoned users, lost protection and transition costs count. Cheap completion can be preferable to a formal cancellation process.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: An option list treated as joint feasibility.
A confirming experiment rejected because the action remains unchanged.
A prototype treated as complete product qualification.
A partial input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Sunk expenditure treated as future benefit.
Private cost preference treated as authority to waive a binding obligation.

positive_controls.argument: Explicit continuation and stopping alternatives make the consequence of learning visible and require transition, beneficiaries and indirect value to be considered.
Prospective continuation, redesign and retirement alternatives ensure architecture findings can affect the real investment rather than merely document a sunk design.
The actual continuation alternatives and their prospective costs identify the risk question an experiment must answer and whether a new test is useful.
The prospective alternatives, transition costs and beneficiary effects make stopping a real evaluated option instead of a rhetorical gate criterion.
Expected future value and transition cost identify which increments merit continuation and when a retained option is no longer worth its upkeep.
Prospective burden, actual use, transition and lost protection provide evidence for retaining, replacing or retiring an optional control.
Continuation, cheap completion, deferral and retirement scenarios separate sunk costs from future consequences and make transition burden explicit.
Real control cost, remaining exposure, transition and option value inform whether an additional control or continued activity is justified.
